investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state and the eval runner never advanced past the scheduling wait.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885), the resulting pod never schedules, the probe times out after ~134–145 s, and no evidence keys are written, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be missing.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable pool is structurally limited to only 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size. If those 2 nodes lose capacity, the entire feature becomes unschedulable.

Tertiary — resource quota or limit-range constraint at the namespace level preventing preemption from reclaiming slots on the 2 eligible nodes (scheduler reports 'No preemption victims found', suggesting existing pods on those nodes are not preemptible or are protected by PodDisruptionBudgets).

Lower confidence — a recent change to node labels, taints, or the pod's affinity spec that reduced the schedulable node pool; no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges so this remains speculative.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state and the eval runner never advanced past the scheduling wait.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885), the resulting pod never schedules, the probe times out after ~134–145 s, and no evidence keys are written, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be missing.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never received any response evidence—leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes. The pod submitted by the eval runner (and by the sibling checks) was left Unschedulable for 134–145 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the agent pod never started, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never returned an agent, no runtime call was made, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime received zero evidence. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real resource-capacity constraint in the production Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
